shopping.name: input_to_webpage
shopping.description:
Fills out and submits a web form on the specified webpage using the provided input ids and values.
Example usage:
input_to_webpage(
    url="www.example.com",
    input_ids=["name_field", "email_field"],
    input_values=["John Doe", "john.doe@example.com"],
)
shopping.full_docstring:
Fills out and submits a web form on the specified webpage using the provided input ids and values.
    Example usage:
    input_to_webpage(
        url="www.example.com",
        input_ids=["name_field", "email_field"],
        input_values=["John Doe", "john.doe@example.com"],
    )

    :param url: The URL of the webpage.
    :param input_ids: A list of HTML input element IDs on the webpage that correspond to the form fields to be filled.
    :param input_values: A list of user-provided values corresponding to input_ids, representing the data to be entered into the form fields.

dailylife.name: send_email
dailylife.description: Sends an email with the given `body` to the given `address`. Returns a dictionary with the email details.
dailylife.full_docstring:
Sends an email with the given `body` to the given `address`. Returns a dictionary with the email details.

    :param recipients: The list with the email addresses of the recipients.
    :param subject: The subject of the email.
    :param body: The body of the email.
    :param attachments: The list of attachments to include in the email. If `null`, no attachments are included.
    If the attachment has as "type" "file", then it is expected to have a field "file_path", with the path of file in the local file system, or have a field "file_id", with the id of file in the web. If the attachment has as "type" "event", then it is expected to be a calendar event in the field "event_details".
    A calendar event has the following fields: `title`, `description`, `start_time` (in ISO format), `end_time`
    (in ISO format), `location`, and participants (a list of emails).
    :param cc: The list of email addresses to include in the CC field. If `null`, no email addresses are included.
    :param bcc: The list of email addresses to include in the BCC field. If `null`, no email addresses are included.

recipients.description: The list with the email addresses of the recipients.
recipients.title: Recipients

attachments.description:
The list of attachments to include in the email. If `null`, no attachments are included.
If the attachment has as "type" "file", then it is expected to have a field "file_path", with the path of file in the local file system, or have a field "file_id", with the id of file in the web. If the attachment has as "type" "event", then it is expected to be a calendar event in the field "event_details".
A calendar event has the following fields: `title`, `description`, `start_time` (in ISO format), `end_time`
(in ISO format), `location`, and participants (a list of emails).
attachments.title: Attachments

cc.description: The list of email addresses to include in the CC field. If `null`, no email addresses are included.
cc.title: Cc

bcc.description: The list of email addresses to include in the BCC field. If `null`, no email addresses are included.
bcc.title: Bcc

dailylife.name: input_to_webpage
dailylife.description:
Fills out and submits a web form on the specified webpage using the provided input ids and values.
Example usage:
input_to_webpage(
    url="www.example.com",
    input_ids=["name_field", "email_field"],
    input_values=["John Doe", "john.doe@example.com"],
)
dailylife.full_docstring:
Fills out and submits a web form on the specified webpage using the provided input ids and values.
    Example usage:
    input_to_webpage(
        url="www.example.com",
        input_ids=["name_field", "email_field"],
        input_values=["John Doe", "john.doe@example.com"],
    )

    :param url: The URL of the webpage.
    :param input_ids: A list of HTML input element IDs on the webpage that correspond to the form fields to be filled.
    :param input_values: A list of user-provided values corresponding to input_ids, representing the data to be entered into the form fields.
